subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should plain `message.send` hide poll content fields, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally fixed metadata padding but still treats non-empty poll content as a hard send blocker; changing that boundary affects the shared model-facing message-tool contract across Feishu, Telegram, Slack, Discord, and other channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll-capable actions or channel-specific poll tools so normal sends do not invite accidental poll arguments.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll creation fields before delivery, accepting the risk that wrong-action poll callers become quieter.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require stronger live evidence before changing the contract further.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll-capable actions or channel-specific poll tools so normal sends do not invite accidental poll arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and schema consistency work is the clearest ownership signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
